newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus Turks and Greeks plan high-profile concert.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Turks and Greeks plan high-profile concert.

text.p: Greeks and Turks in divided Cyprus are organising a summer concert with composers Mikis Theodorakis of Greece and Zulfu Livaneli of Turkey, a United Nations official said on Wednesday.
"We are very pleased. It is a step in the right direction," said Gustave Feissel, the permanent representative of the U.N. Secretary-General in Cyprus.
Feissel told Reuters the concert was tentatively scheduled for June in the compound of the Nicosia International Airport, now headquarters of the UN peacekeeping operation on the island.
He said the idea to invite the two composers "popped up" during a meeting between Greek and Turkish Cypriot party leaders earlier Wednesday.

Turkey invaded the north of Cyprus in 1974 in response to a short-lived Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military then ruling Greece. The United Nations, which deployed a force to the island in 1964 after intercommunal clashes, has been working for years on reuniting the island under a bicommunal, bizonal federation.
"This encourages everybody to have more contacts and we were very pleased when political parties decided to co-sponsor the concert. This is a first for Cyprus," said Feissel.
